title: 12132 Highway Weed Spraying Service (2024 - 2027)
description:
The works consists of up to 3 applications (per annum) of approved herbicide to all of the adopted highway footpaths (circa 1280km consisting of tarmac, slabs, block paving, etc.), back of path edges, walkways, splitter islands, channels, ginnels, edges of all metalled roads and all cobbled areas throughout the borough of Rochdale to provide as near to as possible total weed control.\r
\r
The overall aim is to achieve as close as possible 100% total weed control.\r
\r
To achieve a cleaner more attractive borough, the council is tendering for a weed spraying service to treat specific areas of adopted highway across the borough to prevent the growth of weeds likely to interfere with the highway e.g. create a hazard, cause structural damage, affect drainage, cause a trip hazard or become unsightly.\r
\r
It is proposed that the contractor will deliver three applications of MAFF registered herbicide or other approved chemical as appropriate to Rochdale's adopted highways as specified above.\r
\r
Application should take place as directed by Rochdale Borough Council's Authorised Officer but typically during spring, summer and autumn, at timings which coincide with optimum weed growth.\r

title: NWCH431 - Mini Competition - Rochdale Food Store & Industrial Units
description:
The Council has identified the need to enter into a PCSA with a design and build contractor in order to develop out a food store and 6 adjacent small industrial units. The site is brownfield site in town centre Heywood. An operator for the food store has been identified.

The Council is looking to take the indicative design through the RIBA stages, secure planning permission and produce an indicative cost plan.

The Council proposes to enter into a Pre Contract Service Agreement (PCSA) that would take the layout shared by the operator, work the design through the RIBA stages, secure planning permission and produce a cost plan.

On receipt of these items and the Council determining they are generally able to proceed, a main contract will be executed.

The Council determined that the most appropriate route to market for the design and build project was procuring through the North West Construction Hub (NWCH) Framework.

The NWCH call-off route involves a two-stage process whereby an Expression of Interest stage is used to determine which Contractors are interested in the opportunity. This process ensures that only the Contractors looking to bid are taken through to the Invitation to Tender stage. The expression of interest period ran from 23 April 2025 to 30 April 2025.

Following the Expression of Interest, the NWCH route to market involves a second stage tender - the process is restricted to those Contractors who expressed an interest.

The tender was run through the Chest e-procurement portal with the tender period running from 05 June 2025 to 10 July 2025 (circa 35 days).

The award criteria for scoring was agreed as follows:

Price (30%)

Quality (70%) - breakdown as follows

Method Statements (50%)
There were 4no. scoreable questions (1-5 scoring scale)

Social Value (20%)
There was a quantitative response requirement which formed 10% of the SV criteria and a qualitative method statement question which made up the other 10%.

Following evaluation against the above criteria, it was determined that Tilbury Douglas Limited were the most advantageous tenderer  to the Council.

Estimated Values
PCSA Value: £145,000.00
Main Build: £5,500,000.00

title: Corner Plot - Fire Engineer
description:
OFR have been appointment to provide MEP Services for Stage 2-5 on the works taking place at the Corner Plot, Rochdale Station Square. The roles and requirements will include,

Scope of Works
-Establish the design brief with the Client and confirm the relevant fire safety design 
objectives for the project.
-Confirm any additional design requirements such as insurance.
-Highlight any significant constraints arising from the site such as fire service access, boundary conditions, water supplies and crowd dispersal, etc.
-Identify where a fire engineered (non-standard) approach could add value by 
reducing build costs, shortening the construction programme or enhancing the 
design (e.g. increasing net area, flexibility and functionality).
-Expand on the level of detail provided to align with the developing design. 
Specifically, additional and more detailed advice will be required with regards to 
the fire safety requirements for MEP services and equipment, fire dampers, 
penetrations through fire resisting construction, risers, etc. The Fire Engineer to 
also identify key fire compartmentation interfaces internally and externally.
-Develop the detailed fire strategy report, covering and progressing the same key 
issues, as outlined in the Concept Design stage scope above.
-Detailed advice will be required with regards to the fire safety requirements for 
MEP services and equipment, fire dampers, penetrations through fire resisting 
construction, risers, etc. OFR to also identify key fire compartmentation interfaces 
internally and externally.
-Attend workshops and technical design meetings and comment on design iterations 
to meet the demands of the programme.
-Attend meetings with the approval's authorities, to discuss the outline proposals 
with a view of minimising the approvals risk. Also help to drive the Fire Service 
consultation process at this stage by working with the lead approver to ensure 
consultation takes place as early as possible.
-Review the design documentation produced by others for compatibility with the 
fire strategy, commenting accordingly, and make all reasonable endeavours to 
ensure consultants are producing documentation which complies with the Fire 
Design Strategy Report. This may require the OFR to set up specific fire 
coordination meetings with the other key consultants (Architect, MEP, Structures, 
Accessibility, Façade, Vertical Transportation, CDM).

A modification request was submitted to increase the frequency of project meetings and site visits compared to what was initially agreed.\r

The programme itself had been extended due to multiple issues arising across several partners relating to contractual agreement, procurement, European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) compliance and volatile economic circumstances.\r
\r
CPR 9.3.1(b) permits the council to modify contracts where additional services are required and where a change of contractor cannot be made for economical or technical reasons, or where a change of contractor would cause duplication of costs or an inconvenience for the Council, provided the value of the modification is less than 50% of the original contract value.\r
\r
The value of the contract exceeds the original budget estimated value by £1,861.68 (1.8%).  Due to the complexity of the project an extension of time for circa 4 months is required together with a need for additional meetings at a cost of less 50% of the original contract value.  It would be impractical and result in an unnecessary duplication of costs to change supplier at this juncture in the project.  Reliance on CPR 9.3.1(b) is reasonable in the circumstances.

Following an award (via an exemption due to extreme urgency) for works to re-build a retaining wall that supports Smith Street Car park above the River Roch, issues with ground water were encountered once excavations reached the required depths which hadn't been identified during the previous ground investigations. These issues caused the ground at foundation depth to be weaker than required and resulted in the work on site being stopped whilst an alternative design was determined. The delays to the scheme and changes to the design to rectify these issues increased the contract value. 
Alongside the price increase of the original contract, further works were identified following the commencement of the work, access to the remainder of the wall became accessible and it became apparent that this section of wall was also in poor condition, leaning into the river and bulging in localised areas.
The works for the additional works uncovered by the ground water issues and identification of the issues with a further section of the wall after removal of the initially instructed 30m length of retaining wall, a second exemption was carried out, due to extreme urgency so the contractor currently on site could encompass these additional works into the work they were already carrying out.

Earthworks and grading to formation level.\\r\r
